meta.policy: greedy afterstate + rollout search, topk 4 / 1 playout / budget 120 / playout-max-eval 8 (gate defaults, matches net metadata)
meta.games: 64 fixed-seed games: 4 per ordered pairing over Sligh / White Weenie / The Deck / Counterburn, seeds 9100000+, alternating seats
meta.caveat: search clones carry true hidden state (upstream issue #11), so these games inherit the same information leak the gate numbers do

sligh.style: Burn-first pilot: turn-1 Mountain into face Bolts and Chain Lightnings, Black Vise and Ankh as pseudo-burn, creatures arriving mid-game. Attacks at a 0.75-0.79 phase take-rate when the board is clear (Counterburn, mirror) and races on damage.
sligh.good: Burn allocation reads the board: Bolt on Savannah Lions and Chain Lightning on Order of Leitbur when blockers must die, face when the race is live (seed 9100103). Blocks every phase against the burn decks (1.0 vs Counterburn) and takes the mirror 3/4 by trading burn up.
sligh.mistakes: White Weenie is a 0/4 sweep with a 0.00 attack take-rate — it casts its goblins and never once turns them sideways while Knights kill it. Pure blunders on file: Fireballed its OWN Goblin Balloon Brigade (seed 9100103 turn 20) and Strip-Mined its OWN Mountain on turn 3 (seed 9100200, verified against controller data). 28% of its turns skip a legal land drop, and vs The Deck it walks 4.2 casts per game into two-plus untapped blue lands.

matchups.White Weenie: 0/4, attack take-rate 0.00 — the single worst matchup read in the corpus; it holds a full goblin board home every turn and dies to Knights.
matchups.The Deck: 2/4; attack take-rate sags to 0.40 and 4.2 casts/game go into open counter mana, but burn reach steals two games.
matchups.Counterburn: 2/4 racing; blocks well (1.0) and keeps the burn duel close.
matchups.Sligh mirror: 3/4; the best combat it plays — 4.8 attackers/game and disciplined trades.

examples: seed 9100103 t20: Fireball targets its own Goblin Balloon Brigade
seed 9100200 t3: Strip Mine sacrificed to destroy its own Mountain
seeds 9100100-9100103: 0 attackers declared in four straight WW games

ww.style: Its best seat by far, and the proof the rollout search unlocked aggression: curves Lions into Javelineers into Knights, attacks at a 0.79-0.90 phase take-rate, and closes with Mishra's Factories and Crusade.
ww.good: Steady attack cadence — 8.5 attackers/game in the 4/4 Sligh sweep, and 4/4 vs The Deck by racing the control deck before it sets up. Real card usage: Disenchant on Crusade, Swords to Plowshares on Knights, Strip Mine on opposing Factories.
ww.mistakes: Almost never blocks: 0.00 block take-rate vs Sligh and Counterburn, 23 life conceded to declined blocks across the corpus. Throws lone attackers into bigger boards — six no-damage attacks that lost the creature, three of them in mirror seed 9100503, where it also cast Armageddon on turn 24 while behind on board. The mirror is also its sloppiest resource game: 7 land-skip turns per game.

matchups.Sligh: 4/4 sweep; out-deploys and out-attacks the burn deck before reach matters.
matchups.The Deck: 4/4; 5.8 attackers/game and 9 spells/game — width beats one-for-one answers, the same lesson our main bot's scouting found for weenie decks.
matchups.Counterburn: 3/4; wins the race but blocks nothing (0.00) and gives back chip damage.
matchups.WW mirror: 2/4; suicide-attack habit shows most here (1.2/game) plus heavy land-skipping.

examples: seed 9100503 t6/t20/t24: lone attackers into a bigger board, creature lost for zero damage
seed 9100503 t24: Armageddon while behind on board
seeds 9100400-9100503: 23 life lost across combats where blocks were declined

the-deck.style: It cannot pilot control: swept 0/16. Mulligans average 2.7 per game (seed 9101102 took six, keeping a one-card hand), lands come down late (turns 17/29/33 in seed 9100800), and once the value head reads ~0.0 it passes every phase — the same passivity equilibrium probe.py documented, now isolated to the control seats.
the-deck.good: What little there is: spot removal is aimed correctly (Swords on Serendib Efreet, Disenchant on a Mox), Mind Twist is sized to the legal maximum, and Library of Alexandria hits play on turn 2 when drawn.
the-deck.mistakes: Counterspells stay in hand — 2 casts in 16 games while final hands hold double Counterspell plus Mana Drain (seeds 9100800, 9101100). Win conditions never deploy: Serra Angel appears in the logs only as a hand-size discard (seed 9100800 t27). It discarded Time Walk, Counterspell, and Psionic Blast to hand size in one game (seed 9101402's opposite seat shows the same habit for Counterburn). Worst unspent-mana line of any deck: 19 turns ended with castables in hand. And the purest blunder in the corpus: Ancestral Recall cast targeting the OPPONENT, drawing them three cards (seed 9101102 t13, verified).

matchups.Sligh: 0/4; dies with counters in hand — one game ended at 2 life holding Counterspell x2 + Mana Drain.
matchups.White Weenie: 0/4; never stabilizes, discards Serra Angel instead of casting it.
matchups.The Deck mirror: 0/4 (handcrafted pilots it better); both durdle but handcrafted eventually deploys.
matchups.Counterburn: 0/4 with 2.2 unspent-castable turns/game; burn goes to its face unopposed.

examples: seed 9101102 t13: Ancestral Recall targets the opponent (three free cards)
seed 9100800: lands on t17/t29/t33, Tundra + Serra Angel discarded to hand size, dies holding 2 Counterspells
seed 9101102: six consecutive mulligans to a one-card hand

counterburn.style: Plays it as a pure burn deck: Chain Lightning / Bolt / Psionic Blast to the face, Braingeyser to refill, Earthquake to sweep. The counter half of the deck is dead weight — 2 counterspells cast in 16 games, and it discarded Mana Drain and Counterspell to hand size instead of holding them up.
counterburn.good: Beats The Deck 3/4 by simply burning through — 8 spells/game and geyser refills outpace the answers. Earthquake sweeps at the right X when winning (x=3 max, seed 9101300). Takes the mirror 3/4 on the same plan.
counterburn.mistakes: 1/4 vs Sligh, its supposed prey: after mulling to five it durdles — Braingeyser x=1, Earthquake x=1, and finishers rot in hand (seed 9101202 ended holding two Su-Chi, Serendib Efreet, and a Counterspell at 2 life). Undersizes X when behind (Earthquake x=3 with 4 legal, seed 9101403). The counter-magic non-use is structural: nothing in the feature set represents holding up mana, so the net always prefers casting something now.

matchups.The Deck: 3/4; the burn plan is exactly right here, though 4.0 casts/game go into open counter mana and one loss came from it.
matchups.Sligh: 1/4, the read failure: it durdles with X=1 spells while Sligh races; never blocks, never counters.
matchups.White Weenie: 2/4; Earthquake is the lever, sized right in wins, a turn late in losses.

examples: seed 9101202: loss at 2 life holding Su-Chi x2 + Serendib Efreet + Counterspell
seed 9101402 t13-t17: Time Walk, Counterspell, Psionic Blast discarded to hand size
seed 9101403 t20: Earthquake x=3 with x=4 legal, behind on board

themes: Control-seat passivity: the aggro decks go 20/32, the counter decks 9/32 with The Deck at 0/16. Mulligan spirals (2.7/game), counters and win conditions dying in hand, and 19 unspent-castable turns are one failure: the value net has no representation of held-up mana or future card value.

Matchup-blind combat: attack take-rate swings from 0.90 (WW vs The Deck) to 0.00 (Sligh vs WW) with nothing in between learned per-matchup; blocks are declined at a 0.00-0.50 rate for 48 life conceded corpus-wide.

Self-targeting blunders: Ancestral Recall at the opponent, Fireball at its own goblin, Strip Mine on its own Mountain — enumerated targets are scored purely by afterstate value, and the 1-ply screen misprices symmetric effects the playout never revisits.
